source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

session_uid.caption: Session ID
session_uid.description: The native session identifier reported by the CLI (ACP session). Not a Journal run identifier.

turn_uid.caption: Prompt Turn ID
turn_uid.description: The native identifier of the prompt turn, when the source reports one.

response_uid.caption: Model Response ID
response_uid.description: The model provider's identifier of the model response (for example the Anthropic message id), when the source reports one. Never a source-local item identifier, and absent when no response identifier is reported.

tool_call_uid.caption: Tool Call ID
tool_call_uid.description: The native identifier of the tool call request. Absent when the source does not report one for the record.

identity_basis_id.caption: Identity Basis ID
identity_basis_id.description: What kind of identifier tool_call_uid is, when a declared rule states it.

1.caption: Model-facing call identifier
1.description: The identifier the model's own tool request carried, as the source reports it.

2.caption: Stream-local item identifier
2.description: An identifier the CLI's output stream assigns to its own items. It is unique only within one source artifact of one Journal invocation (journal.run_uid, journal.invocation_index, source_ref.artifact): an equal value in another invocation is another item. The model-facing call or response identifier is not reported.

tool_name.caption: Tool Name
tool_name.description: The exact tool name as the source reports it. Never normalized, and absent when the source reports no name: a family or item type (tool_family) is not a name.

tool_family.caption: Tool Family
tool_family.description: The source's own family or item type of a tool activity, exactly as reported (for example the Codex exec item types mcp_tool_call, web_search, collab_tool_call and file_change). Not a tool name.

tool_namespace.caption: Tool Namespace
tool_namespace.description: The namespace the source reports beside the tool name, such as the MCP server of an MCP tool. Absent when the source reports none; never derived from the tool name.

tool_kind_id.caption: Tool Kind ID
tool_kind_id.description: The ACP tool kind of the requested tool activity, assigned by a declared mapping rule named in tool_kind_basis. A kind describes the request; it is not evidence of an operating-system effect.

tool_kind.caption: Tool Kind
tool_kind.description: The ACP tool kind caption, sibling of tool_kind_id.

tool_kind_basis.caption: Tool Kind Basis
tool_kind_basis.description: The declared mapping rule that assigned tool_kind_id: a table over tool names the source reports for its own tools, a table over source families, or a reviewed namespace binding. A name under another namespace (for example an MCP tool named like a built-in tool) never takes the built-in's kind. Shell command parsing is not a permitted basis.

arguments.caption: Tool Arguments
arguments.description: The tool request arguments exactly as the source reported them (object, string or other JSON value).

tool_result.caption: Tool Result
tool_result.description: The observed result of a tool call as the source returned it.

tool_operation.caption: Operation
tool_operation.description: A separately reported operation executed within a tool call (for example one command of a multi-command exec).

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The request/result lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example ACTIVE, DONE, completed).

permission_decision.caption: Permission Decision
permission_decision.description: A permission decision reported by the source at its reported scope.

status_basis_id.caption: Status Basis ID
status_basis_id.description: Whether status_id was reported by the source, derived by a declared Journal rule, or could not be derived.

derivation.caption: Derivation
derivation.description: Identifier of the declared rule and inputs used to derive a value.

mcp.caption: MCP Observation
mcp.description: What this event observed of a Model Context Protocol interaction: protocol revision and basis, the addressed server and tool with their bases, and typed protocol objects (complete, partial CLI projection or schema example).

assembly.caption: Assembly
assembly.description: Present in a finally assembled file: this event's assembly role and evidence.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Native record fields not represented elsewhere on the event (residual).

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

time_dt.caption: Event Time
time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The Account object contains details about the account that initiated or performed a specific activity within a system or application. Additionally, the Account object refers to logical Cloud and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) based containers such as AWS Accounts, Azure Subscriptions, Oracle Cloud Compartments, Google Cloud Projects, and otherwise.
account.name: account

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the account (e.g. GCP Project name , Linux Account name or AWS Account name).

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the account (e.g. AWS Account ID , OCID , GCP Project ID , Azure Subscription ID , Google Workspace Customer ID , or M365 Tenant UID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

is_disabled.caption: Disabled
is_disabled.description: Indicates if the account is disabled.

is_locked.caption: Locked
is_locked.description: Indicates if the account is locked. For example, due to the amount of failed logins.

is_on_premises_sync_enabled.caption: On-Premises Sync Enabled
is_on_premises_sync_enabled.description: Indicates whether synchronization with an on-premises directory service is enabled. For example, Microsoft Entra Connect.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the account.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the account.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The account type, normalized to the caption of 'account_type_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The account type is not mapped.

6.caption: Azure AD Account
6.description: Note: The new product name for Azure AD is Microsoft Entra ID.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The Actor object contains details about the user, role, application, service, or process that initiated or performed a specific activity. Note that Actor is not the threat actor of a campaign but may be part of a campaign. When the initiator of the activity is an autonomous AI agent, apply the ai_operation profile and populate ai_operation.ai_agent rather than describing the agent here.
actor.name: actor

app_name.caption: Application Name
app_name.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process if present.

app_uid.caption: Application ID
app_uid.description: The unique identifier of the client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process.pid or process.uid if present.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that application is distinct from the process if present.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

iam_role.caption: IAM Role
iam_role.description: The actor's role, or as an alternative to user or process when the role is serving as a security principal for the operation that initiated the activity.

idp.caption: Identity Provider
idp.description: This object describes details about the Identity Provider used.

invoked_by.caption: Invoked by
invoked_by.description: The name of the service that invoked the activity as described in the event.

process.caption: Process
process.description: The process that initiated the activity.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session from which the activity was initiated.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that initiated the activity or the user context from which the activity was initiated.

advisory.caption: Advisory
advisory.description: The Advisory object represents publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities defined in a Security advisory. e.g. Microsoft KB Article, Apple Security Advisory, or a GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA)
advisory.name: advisory

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The vendors classification of the Advisory.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the Advisory record was created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the Advisory Record.

install_state.caption: Install State
install_state.description: The install state of the Advisory.

install_state_id.caption: Install State ID
install_state_id.description: The normalized install state ID of the Advisory.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The normalized install state is unknown.

1.caption: Installed
1.description: The item is installed.

2.caption: Not Installed
2.description: The item is not installed.

3.caption: Installed Pending Reboot
3.description: The item is installed pending reboot operation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The install state is not mapped. See the install_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_superseded.caption: The patch is superseded.
is_superseded.description: The Advisory has been replaced by another.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the Advisory record was last updated.

os.caption: OS
os.description: The operating system the Advisory applies to.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

related_cves.caption: Related CVEs
related_cves.description: A list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers related to the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) identifiers related to the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes for the Advisory. Usually populated for a KB Article patch.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The Advisory link from the source vendor.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the Advisory.

uid.caption: Advisory ID
uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the advisory or disclosed vulnerability, e.g, GHSA-5mrr-rgp6-x4gr.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the Advisory record was created.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the Advisory record was last updated.

affected_code.caption: Affected Code
affected_code.description: The Affected Code object describes details about a code block identified as vulnerable.
affected_code.name: affected_code

end_column.caption: End Column
end_column.description: The column number of the last part of the assessed code identified as vulnerable.

end_line.caption: End Line
end_line.description: The line number of the last line of code block identified as vulnerable.

file.caption: File
file.description: Details about the file that contains the affected code block.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: Details about the user that owns the affected file.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

rule.caption: Related Rule
rule.description: Details about the specific rule, e.g., those defined as part of a larger policy, that triggered the finding.

start_column.caption: Start Column
start_column.description: The column number of the first part of the assessed code identified as vulnerable.

start_line.caption: Start Line
start_line.description: The line number of the first line of code block identified as vulnerable.

affected_package.caption: Affected Software Package
affected_package.description: The Affected Package object describes details about a software package identified as affected by a vulnerability/vulnerabilities.
affected_package.name: affected_package

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

license_url.caption: Software License URL
license_url.description: The URL pointing to the license applied on package or software. This is typically a LICENSE.md file within a repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

package_manager.caption: Package Manager
package_manager.description: The software packager manager utilized to manage a package on a system, e.g. npm, yum, dpkg etc.

package_manager_url.caption: Package Manager URL
package_manager_url.description: The URL of the package or library at the package manager, or the specific URL or URI of an internal package manager link such as AWS CodeArtifact or Artifactory.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The link to the specific library or package such as within GitHub, this is different from the link to the package manager where the library or package is hosted.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Application
1.description: An application software package.

2.caption: Operating System
2.description: An operating system software package.

uid.caption: Package UID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the package or library reported by the source tool. E.g., the libId within the sbom field of an OX Security Issue or the SPDX components.*.bom-ref.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The software package version.

fixed_in_version.caption: Fixed In Version
fixed_in_version.description: The software package version in which a reported vulnerability was patched/fixed.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The installation path of the affected package.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

agent.caption: Agent
agent.description: An Agent (also known as a Sensor) is typically installed on an Operating System (OS) and serves as a specialized software component that can be designed to monitor, detect, collect, archive, or take action. These activities and possible actions are defined by the upstream system controlling the Agent and its intended purpose. For instance, an Agent can include Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) agents, backup/disaster recovery sensors, Application Performance Monitoring or profiling sensors, and similar software.
agent.name: agent

name.caption: Agent Name
name.description: The name of the agent or sensor. For example: AWS SSM Agent.

policies.caption: Agent Policies
policies.description: Describes the various policies that may be applied or enforced by an agent or sensor. E.g., Conditional Access, prevention, auto-update, tamper protection, destination configuration, etc.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The normalized caption of the type_id value for the agent or sensor. In the case of 'Other' or 'Unknown', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized representation of an agent or sensor. E.g., EDR, vulnerability management, APM, backup & recovery, etc.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Endpoint Detection and Response
1.description: Any EDR sensor or agent. Or any tool that provides similar threat detection, anti-malware, anti-ransomware, or similar capabilities. E.g., Crowdstrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Wazuh.

2.caption: Data Loss Prevention
2.description: Any DLP sensor or agent. Or any tool that provides similar data classification, data loss detection, and/or data loss prevention capabilities. E.g., Forcepoint DLP, Microsoft Purview, Symantec DLP.

3.caption: Backup & Recovery
3.description: Any agent or sensor that provides backups, archival, or recovery capabilities. E.g., Azure Backup, AWS Backint Agent.

4.caption: Performance Monitoring & Observability
4.description: Any agent or sensor that provides Application Performance Monitoring (APM), active tracing, profiling, or other observability use cases and optionally forwards the logs. E.g., New Relic Agent, Datadog Agent, Azure Monitor Agent.

5.caption: Vulnerability Management
5.description: Any agent or sensor that provides vulnerability management or scanning capabilities. E.g., Qualys VMDR, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Crowdstrike Spotlight, Amazon Inspector Agent.

6.caption: Log Forwarding
6.description: Any agent or sensor that forwards logs to a 3rd party storage system such as a data lake or SIEM. E.g., Splunk Universal Forwarder, Tenzir, FluentBit, Amazon CloudWatch Agent, Amazon Kinesis Agent.

7.caption: Mobile Device Management
7.description: Any agent or sensor responsible for providing Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Mobile Enterprise Management (MEM) capabilities. E.g., JumpCloud Agent, Esper Agent, Jamf Pro binary.

8.caption: Configuration Management
8.description: Any agent or sensor that provides configuration management of a device, such as scanning for software, license management, or applying configurations. E.g., AWS Systems Manager Agent, Flexera, ServiceNow MID Server.

9.caption: Remote Access
9.description: Any agent or sensor that provides remote access capabilities to a device. E.g., BeyondTrust, Amazon Systems Manager Agent, Verkada Agent.

uid.caption: Agent ID
uid.description: The UID of the agent or sensor, sometimes known as a Sensor ID or aid.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate Agent ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the agent or sensor, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The company or author who created the agent or sensor. For example: Crowdstrike.

version.caption: Agent Version
version.description: The semantic version of the agent or sensor, e.g., 7.101.50.0.

agentic_cli/assembly_conflict.caption: Assembly Conflict
agentic_cli/assembly_conflict.description: Disagreeing reports of one field of one logical entity, each kept with its occurrence; resolution states whether a declared authority selected one or the field stays unresolved.
agentic_cli/assembly_conflict.name: assembly_conflict

field_pointer.caption: Field Pointer
field_pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer into the consolidated event.

observed_values.caption: Observed Values
observed_values.description: Each disagreeing value with its occurrence: [{occurrence_uid, value}].

resolution.caption: Resolution
resolution.description: unresolved, or the declared authority that selected the canonical value.

agentic_cli/assembly_record.caption: Assembly Record
agentic_cli/assembly_record.description: How final assembly placed this event: a canonical event observed by one source, a consolidated canonical event built from several sources' observations of one logical entity at one lifecycle stage, or a supporting observation kept as evidence and never counted again. entity_uid names the logical entity in its declared identity namespace; occurrence_uid names the source occurrence (artifact, record and emit ordinal).
agentic_cli/assembly_record.name: assembly_record

assembly_role_id.caption: Assembly Role ID
assembly_role_id.description: The event's role in an assembled file. Canonical consumers read roles 1 and 3; role 2 is evidence and never counted as an execution.

1.caption: Canonical single observation
1.description: The only observation of its entity and stage among the declared sources.

2.caption: Supporting observation
2.description: One source's observation of an entity whose consolidated canonical event is in the same file.

3.caption: Consolidated canonical
3.description: The canonical event of an entity and stage that several sources observed, built from their compatible fields with per-field evidence.

entity_uid.caption: Entity ID
entity_uid.description: The logical entity and lifecycle stage in its declared identity namespace (for example tool_call/started/copilot.toolCallId:call_1).

occurrence_uid.caption: Occurrence ID
occurrence_uid.description: A source occurrence: artifact, one-based record index and the emit ordinal of the event within that record (artifact#record/ordinal).

relation_class_id.caption: Relation Class ID
relation_class_id.description: How the observations of one entity, or of one field, relate.

2.caption: Representation only
2.description: Equal values spelled differently (1 and 1.0).

3.caption: One richer
3.description: One observation carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

4.caption: Each richer
4.description: Each carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

5.caption: Conflicting
5.description: Two observations report different values for one field.

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded
8.description: A provisional observation of a quantity that a final observation of the same quantity (same scope, aggregation and model) supersedes: the canonical event carries the final one and the provisional one stays on its supporting observation, never counted again.

observation_refs.caption: Observation References
observation_refs.description: The source occurrences a consolidated event was built from.

field_evidence.caption: Field Evidence
field_evidence.description: Per-field evidence of a consolidated event for every field whose observations are not identical.

assembly_conflicts.caption: Assembly Conflicts
assembly_conflicts.description: Fields whose observations disagree, each value with its occurrence.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rule, join keys or reason behind a classification, derivation or fallback.

agentic_cli/attribution.caption: Attribution
agentic_cli/attribution.description: The declared outcome of associating a fact with an owner, and how the candidates were obtained (reported identifier or derived by rule).
agentic_cli/attribution.name: attribution

outcome_id.caption: Attribution Outcome ID
outcome_id.description: Whether the owner of a fact could be established from the source.

1.caption: Unique
1.description: Exactly one owner is established by the declared join keys.

2.caption: Ambiguous
2.description: More than one candidate owner satisfies the declared join keys; the fact is attached at the enclosing scope only.

3.caption: Unattributed
3.description: The source provides no key to any owner; the fact is retained at its reported scope.

candidates.caption: Candidate Owners
candidates.description: Identifiers of the candidate owners considered.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rule, join keys or reason behind a classification, derivation or fallback.

scope_uid.caption: Scope ID
scope_uid.description: Identifier of the scope within which candidates were considered (for example a turn id).

method_id.caption: Attribution Method ID
method_id.description: How the candidate owners of an attribution were obtained: from an identifier the source record itself reports at the declared path, or by a declared derivation rule (for example text containment within a scope). A derived association is never a reported parent identifier.

1.caption: Reported identifier
1.description: The source record names the owner at the declared path.

2.caption: Derived by rule
2.description: Candidates were computed by the declared rule named in basis; the source reports no owner identifier.

agentic_cli/cache_write_tier.caption: Cache Write Tier
agentic_cli/cache_write_tier.description: One source-reported part of cache_write_tokens: a retention or pricing tier and its token count. Tier counts are parts of their parent total, never additional usage.
agentic_cli/cache_write_tier.name: cache_write_tier

tier.caption: Tier
tier.description: A tier exactly as the source names it (for example the member ephemeral_1h_input_tokens of Claude's cache_creation).

native_pointers.caption: Native Pointers
native_pointers.description: The RFC 6901 pointer of the native member, in the observation's data.

agentic_cli/cli_agent.caption: CLI Agent
agentic_cli/cli_agent.description: An agentic CLI observed by Agent Journal, defined by this extension (since 0.4.0-prototype it does not extend the core ai_agent, whose framework-agent vocabulary does not describe an agentic CLI). product identifies the CLI product and version; name is the product name; version is the CLI version; instance_uid is the native session id; uid is set only when a source reports a stable logical agent identity. Launch settings and source references belong to the run manifest and source_ref, not to this object.
agentic_cli/cli_agent.name: cli_agent

name.caption: Name
name.description: The CLI product name.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CLI version, as the source reports it or as the adapter's documented discovery found it.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A stable logical agent identity, set only when a source reports one; never the product name or a session id.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The native session identifier of this invocation.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The CLI product and version that produced the observed records.

agentic_cli/content_block.caption: Content Block
agentic_cli/content_block.description: One ordered content block of a message. data holds the exact native block.
agentic_cli/content_block.name: content_block

block_index.caption: Block Index
block_index.description: Zero-based position of the block within the source record's content array.

block_type.caption: Block Type
block_type.description: The native block type string, exactly as reported.

block_kind_id.caption: Block Kind ID
block_kind_id.description: ACP-style content kind of the block, assigned by a declared mapping rule.

reasoning_form_id.caption: Reasoning Form ID
reasoning_form_id.description: What a reasoning content block holds, as a declared rule establishes it from the source. Absent when the source does not establish it.

1.caption: Full reasoning
1.description: The model's reasoning text as produced.

2.caption: Summary
2.description: A summary of the model's reasoning, not its full text.

3.caption: Redacted
3.description: The source reports that reasoning occurred but withholds its text (for example encrypted or redacted reasoning).

text.caption: Text
text.description: The text content of a block when the source reports text.

text_update_id.caption: Text Update ID
text_update_id.description: How this block's text relates to the text of the same content item (item_uid) or response (response_uid) that earlier events of the same source artifact reported, as a declared rule establishes it. Absent when no rule states it; a consumer then assumes neither.

1.caption: Increment
1.description: The text continues the item's text: the item's text is the concatenation, in journal.sequence order, of the texts of its Increment blocks. An increment is not by itself asserted to be the whole text, and the assembled text is never concatenated with a whole text reported elsewhere (for example a turn's own response).

2.caption: Snapshot
2.description: The text is the item's whole text as of this record: it replaces any earlier view of the item and is never concatenated with one.

tool_call_uid.caption: Tool Call ID
tool_call_uid.description: The native identifier of the tool call request. Absent when the source does not report one for the record.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native block exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/cost_observation.caption: Cost Observation
agentic_cli/cost_observation.description: A reported cost or billing quantity with its scope, basis and source: a monetary total with its currency, or a non-monetary billing quantity (premium requests, a model cost multiplier, nano-AIU, credits) with its quantity kind and unit. Quantities of different kinds are never added together or read as money. Present only when a source reported one. A per-model quantity names its model (model_ref).
agentic_cli/cost_observation.name: cost_observation

total_cost.caption: Total Cost
total_cost.description: The reported cost total exactly as reported.

currency.caption: Currency
currency.description: The ISO 4217 currency of a monetary amount; absent for a billing quantity that is not money.

quantity_kind_id.caption: Quantity Kind ID
quantity_kind_id.description: What a cost observation counts. Different kinds are never added together, and only a Monetary amount has a currency.

1.caption: Monetary amount
1.description: Money in the stated currency.

2.caption: Premium requests
2.description: A count of premium requests the CLI reports as consumed.

3.caption: Model cost multiplier
3.description: A per-call model multiplier, or a sum of such multipliers, that a vendor reports for billing; not money and not a request count.

4.caption: Nano-AIU
4.description: Nano AI units a vendor reports.

5.caption: Credits
5.description: Account credits a vendor reports.

quantity_kind.caption: Quantity Kind
quantity_kind.description: The caption of quantity_kind_id, or the source's own name for 99 Other.

quantity_unit.caption: Quantity Unit
quantity_unit.description: The unit a non-monetary billing quantity is stated in, as the source names it.

aggregation_id.caption: Aggregation ID
aggregation_id.description: How the observation's components accumulate, independently of its scope (scope_id) and finality (usage_status_id).

1.caption: Scope total
1.description: The consumption of exactly the observation's scope unit (for example one model response); observations of distinct units of that scope are disjoint.

2.caption: Cumulative snapshot
2.description: A running total of the scope unit from its start up to the point of observation. It may include consumption before this capture began and is not the unit's completed total; two snapshots of one unit overlap and are never summed.

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation. 99 Other names, in its sibling scope, a unit the source defines that no other value describes.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A unit the source itself defines, which none of the other scopes describes; the sibling scope names it (for example Conversation step). It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation).

scope.caption: Scope
scope.description: Caption sibling of scope_id; for 99 Other, the name of the source-defined unit.

model_ref.caption: Model Reference
model_ref.description: The model the quantity belongs to, when the source reports it per model (a per-model cost); a cost observation of one quantity kind, scope and unit is distinct per model.

cost_basis.caption: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: The source's reported pricing basis, if any (for example list).

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native cost-bearing value or object exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/error_info.caption: Error Information
agentic_cli/error_info.description: One reported error with the layer that reported it: a JSON-RPC protocol error response, a tool result that reports an error (MCP isError), a failure the CLI reports for a tool call, a CLI or process failure, or Journal's own capture failure. The layers stay distinct; an absent error is not a success and an absent isError is not false.
agentic_cli/error_info.name: error_info

1.caption: JSON-RPC protocol error
1.description: An MCP or JSON-RPC error response (code, message, data).

2.caption: Tool result error
2.description: A tool result that reports an error as its content (MCP isError true).

3.caption: CLI-reported tool failure
3.description: The CLI reports that a tool call failed, without establishing which protocol layer failed.

4.caption: CLI or process failure
4.description: The CLI or its process reports a failure outside a tool call.

5.caption: Capture failure
5.description: Journal's own acquisition or persistence failed; not a vendor report.

error_code.caption: Error Code
error_code.description: An error code exactly as reported, keeping its JSON type (a JSON-RPC integer, a CLI string).

message.caption: Message
message.description: The error message exactly as reported.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Error data exactly as reported.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rule, join keys or reason behind a classification, derivation or fallback.

agentic_cli/field_evidence.caption: Field Evidence
agentic_cli/field_evidence.description: Which occurrences supplied one field of a consolidated event and how their reports relate: a single source, identical, differing only in representation, or conflicting (the value then absent unless a declared authority selected one).
agentic_cli/field_evidence.name: field_evidence

field_pointer.caption: Field Pointer
field_pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer into the consolidated event.

relation_class_id.caption: Relation Class ID
relation_class_id.description: How the observations of one entity, or of one field, relate.

2.caption: Representation only
2.description: Equal values spelled differently (1 and 1.0).

3.caption: One richer
3.description: One observation carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

4.caption: Each richer
4.description: Each carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

5.caption: Conflicting
5.description: Two observations report different values for one field.

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded
8.description: A provisional observation of a quantity that a final observation of the same quantity (same scope, aggregation and model) supersedes: the canonical event carries the final one and the provisional one stays on its supporting observation, never counted again.

occurrence_uids.caption: Occurrence IDs
occurrence_uids.description: The occurrences that reported a field.

selection_basis.caption: Selection Basis
selection_basis.description: Why the canonical value of a field is the one shown (single source, equal reports, a declared authority).

agentic_cli/journal_provenance.caption: Journal Provenance
agentic_cli/journal_provenance.description: Agent Journal's provenance for a transformed or generated event. Invariant per-run facts (producer, capture time, contract hash) are stored once in run.json under shared and are reached through run_uid and contract_uid; they appear on an event only in a self-contained export.
agentic_cli/journal_provenance.name: journal_provenance

run_uid.caption: Journal Run ID
run_uid.description: The Agent Journal run identifier that owns this event.

invocation_index.caption: Invocation Index
invocation_index.description: Zero-based index of the CLI invocation within the Journal run.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Journal's event sequence within the run; occurrence order, never clock order.

producer.caption: Producer
producer.description: The Journal producer (transformer) that wrote the event; distinct from the originating CLI in metadata.product.

contract_uid.caption: Mapping Contract ID
contract_uid.description: Identifier of the mapping contract that produced this event, resolved through run.json.

rule_uid.caption: Mapping Rule ID
rule_uid.description: The contract rule that produced this event (0.5.0-prototype; earlier packages carry unmapped.rule_id).

contract_sha256.caption: Mapping Contract SHA-256
contract_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the mapping contract document embedded in run.json.

capture_time.caption: Capture Time
capture_time.description: When Journal observed or transformed the record, as epoch milliseconds.

capture_time_text.caption: Capture Time Text
capture_time_text.description: Journal's capture/transformation time at full precision, RFC 3339.

time_basis_id.caption: Time Basis ID
time_basis_id.description: How the event's time was established.

1.caption: Source record
1.description: The source record reports a timestamp; time is that value and metadata.original_time holds its text.

2.caption: Earliest available fallback
2.description: The record reports no time; time is the latest preceding source-reported time in the same occurrence sequence, or the capture start when none precedes. basis names which.

3.caption: Capture observation
3.description: The event is a Journal observation; time is when Journal observed it.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: Detail for the time basis (for example which preceding record supplied the fallback time).

capture_time_dt.caption: Capture Time
capture_time_dt.description: When Journal observed or transformed the record, as epoch milliseconds.

mcp_cache_scope.caption: MCP Cache Scope
mcp_cache_scope.description:
MCP member `cacheScope` (required by the protocol): Indicates the intended scope of the cached response, analogous to HTTP
`Cache-Control: public` vs `Cache-Control: private`.

- `"public"`: The response does not contain user-specific data. Any
  client or intermediary (e.g., shared gateway, caching proxy) MAY cache
  the response and serve it across authorization contexts.
- `"private"`: The response MAY be cached and reused only within the
  same authorization context. Caches MUST NOT be shared across
  authorization contexts (e.g., a different access token requires a
  different cache).

mcp_result_type.caption: MCP Result Type
mcp_result_type.description:
MCP member `resultType` (required by the protocol): Indicates the type of the result, which allows the client to determine
how to parse the result object.

Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field.
For backward compatibility, when a client receives a result from a
server implementing an earlier protocol version (which does not include
`resultType`), the client MUST treat the absent field as `"complete"`.

mcp_ttl_ms.caption: MCP Ttl Ms
mcp_ttl_ms.description:
MCP member `ttlMs` (required by the protocol): A hint from the server indicating how long (in milliseconds) the
client MAY cache this response before re-fetching. Semantics are
analogous to HTTP Cache-Control max-age.

- If 0, The response SHOULD be considered immediately stale,
  The client MAY re-fetch every time the result is needed.
- If positive, the client SHOULD consider the result fresh for this many
  milliseconds after receiving the response.

mcp_is_error.caption: MCP Is Error
mcp_is_error.description:
MCP member `isError`: Whether the tool call ended in an error.

If not set, this is assumed to be false (the call was successful).

Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result
object, with `isError` set to true, _not_ as an MCP protocol-level error
response. Otherwise, the LLM would not be able to see that an error occurred
and self-correct.

However, any errors in _finding_ the tool, an error indicating that the
server does not support tool calls, or any other exceptional conditions,
should be reported as an MCP error response.

agentic_cli/mcp_cancelled_notification.description:
This notification can be sent by either side to indicate that it is cancelling a previously-issued request.

The request SHOULD still be in-flight, but due to communication latency, it is always possible that this notification MAY arrive after the request has already finished.

This notification indicates that the result will be unused, so any associated processing SHOULD cease.

A client MUST NOT attempt to cancel its `initialize` request.

For task cancellation, use the `tasks/cancel` request instead of this notification. Generated from the pinned MCP schema (2025-11-25 CancelledNotification; 2026-07-28 CancelledNotification).

agentic_cli/mcp_client_notification__202.caption: MCP Client Notification 2026 07 28
agentic_cli/mcp_client_notification__202.description:
This notification is sent by the client to indicate that it is cancelling a request it previously issued.

On stdio, the server also sends this notification, solely to terminate a {@link SubscriptionsListenRequestsubscriptions/listen} stream: it references the ID of the `subscriptions/listen` request that opened the stream. Servers MUST NOT use this notification to cancel any other request.

The request SHOULD still be in-flight, but due to communication latency, it is always possible that this notification MAY arrive after the request has already finished.

This notification indicates that the result will be unused, so any associated processing SHOULD cease. Generated from the pinned MCP schema (2026-07-28 ClientNotification).

The client MAY ignore this request.

Default is "none". Values "thisServer" and "allServers" are soft-deprecated. Servers SHOULD only use these values if the client
declares ClientCapabilities.sampling.context. These values may be removed in future spec releases.

mcp_max_tokens.caption: MCP Max Tokens
mcp_max_tokens.description:
MCP member `maxTokens` (required by the protocol): The requested maximum number of tokens to sample (to prevent runaway completions).

The client MAY choose to sample fewer tokens than the requested maximum.

mcp_metadata.caption: MCP Metadata
mcp_metadata.description: MCP member `metadata`: Optional metadata to pass through to the LLM provider. The format of this metadata is provider-specific.

mcp_model_preferences.caption: MCP Model Preferences
mcp_model_preferences.description: MCP member `modelPreferences`: The server's preferences for which model to select. The client MAY ignore these preferences.

mcp_system_prompt.caption: MCP System Prompt
mcp_system_prompt.description: MCP member `systemPrompt`: An optional system prompt the server wants to use for sampling. The client MAY modify or omit this prompt.

mcp_task_metadata.caption: MCP Task Metadata
mcp_task_metadata.description:
MCP member `task`: If specified, the caller is requesting task-augmented execution for this request.
The request will return a CreateTaskResult immediately, and the actual result can be
retrieved later via tasks/result.

Task augmentation is subject to capability negotiation - receivers MUST declare support
for task augmentation of specific request types in their capabilities.

mcp_tool_choice.caption: MCP Tool Choice
mcp_tool_choice.description:
MCP member `toolChoice`: Controls how the model uses tools.
The client MUST return an error if this field is provided but ClientCapabilities.sampling.tools is not declared.
Default is `{ mode: "auto" }`.

mcp_tool_list.caption: MCP Tool List
mcp_tool_list.description:
MCP member `tools`: Tools that the model may use during generation.
The client MUST return an error if this field is provided but ClientCapabilities.sampling.tools is not declared.

mcp_cache_scope.caption: MCP Cache Scope
mcp_cache_scope.description:
MCP member `cacheScope` (required by the protocol): Indicates the intended scope of the cached response, analogous to HTTP
`Cache-Control: public` vs `Cache-Control: private`.

- `"public"`: The response does not contain user-specific data. Any
  client or intermediary (e.g., shared gateway, caching proxy) MAY cache
  the response and serve it across authorization contexts.
- `"private"`: The response MAY be cached and reused only within the
  same authorization context. Caches MUST NOT be shared across
  authorization contexts (e.g., a different access token requires a
  different cache).

mcp_server_capabilities.caption: MCP Server Capabilities
mcp_server_capabilities.description: MCP member `capabilities` (required by the protocol): The capabilities of the server.

mcp_instructions.caption: MCP Instructions
mcp_instructions.description:
MCP member `instructions`: Natural-language guidance describing the server and its features.

This can be used by clients to improve an LLM's understanding of
available tools (e.g., by including it in a system prompt). It should
focus on information that helps the model use the server effectively
and should not duplicate information already in tool descriptions.

mcp_result_type.caption: MCP Result Type
mcp_result_type.description:
MCP member `resultType` (required by the protocol): Indicates the type of the result, which allows the client to determine
how to parse the result object.

Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field.
For backward compatibility, when a client receives a result from a
server implementing an earlier protocol version (which does not include
`resultType`), the client MUST treat the absent field as `"complete"`.

mcp_supported_versions.caption: MCP Supported Versions
mcp_supported_versions.description:
MCP member `supportedVersions` (required by the protocol): MCP Protocol Versions this server supports. The client should choose a
version from this list for use in subsequent requests.

mcp_ttl_ms.caption: MCP Ttl Ms
mcp_ttl_ms.description:
MCP member `ttlMs` (required by the protocol): A hint from the server indicating how long (in milliseconds) the
client MAY cache this response before re-fetching. Semantics are
analogous to HTTP Cache-Control max-age.

- If 0, The response SHOULD be considered immediately stale,
  The client MAY re-fetch every time the result is needed.
- If positive, the client SHOULD consider the result fresh for this many
  milliseconds after receiving the response.

MCP member `sizes`: Optional array of strings that specify sizes at which the icon can be used.
Each string should be in WxH format (e.g., `"48x48"`, `"96x96"`) or `"any"` for scalable formats like SVG.

If not provided, the client should assume that the icon can be used at any size.

mcp_src.caption: MCP Src
mcp_src.description:
MCP member `src` (required by the protocol): A standard URI pointing to an icon resource. May be an HTTP/HTTPS URL or a
`data:` URI with Base64-encoded image data.

Consumers SHOULD takes steps to ensure URLs serving icons are from the
same domain as the client/server or a trusted domain.

Consumers SHOULD take appropriate precautions when consuming SVGs as they can contain
executable JavaScript.

mcp_theme.caption: MCP Theme
mcp_theme.description:
MCP member `theme`: Optional specifier for the theme this icon is designed for. `light` indicates
the icon is designed to be used with a light background, and `dark` indicates
the icon is designed to be used with a dark background.

If not provided, the client should assume the icon can be used with any theme.

- **Pagination**: Invalid or expired cursor values
- **Logging**: Invalid log level
- **Elicitation**: Server requests an elicitation mode not declared in client capabilities
- **Sampling**: Missing tool result or tool results mixed with other content Generated from the pinned MCP schema (2026-07-28 InvalidParamsError).

mcp_cache_scope.caption: MCP Cache Scope
mcp_cache_scope.description:
MCP member `cacheScope` (required by the protocol): Indicates the intended scope of the cached response, analogous to HTTP
`Cache-Control: public` vs `Cache-Control: private`.

- `"public"`: The response does not contain user-specific data. Any
  client or intermediary (e.g., shared gateway, caching proxy) MAY cache
  the response and serve it across authorization contexts.
- `"private"`: The response MAY be cached and reused only within the
  same authorization context. Caches MUST NOT be shared across
  authorization contexts (e.g., a different access token requires a
  different cache).

mcp_result_type.caption: MCP Result Type
mcp_result_type.description:
MCP member `resultType` (required by the protocol): Indicates the type of the result, which allows the client to determine
how to parse the result object.

Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field.
For backward compatibility, when a client receives a result from a
server implementing an earlier protocol version (which does not include
`resultType`), the client MUST treat the absent field as `"complete"`.

mcp_ttl_ms.caption: MCP Ttl Ms
mcp_ttl_ms.description:
MCP member `ttlMs` (required by the protocol): A hint from the server indicating how long (in milliseconds) the
client MAY cache this response before re-fetching. Semantics are
analogous to HTTP Cache-Control max-age.

- If 0, The response SHOULD be considered immediately stale,
  The client MAY re-fetch every time the result is needed.
- If positive, the client SHOULD consider the result fresh for this many
  milliseconds after receiving the response.

mcp_cache_scope.caption: MCP Cache Scope
mcp_cache_scope.description:
MCP member `cacheScope` (required by the protocol): Indicates the intended scope of the cached response, analogous to HTTP
`Cache-Control: public` vs `Cache-Control: private`.

- `"public"`: The response does not contain user-specific data. Any
  client or intermediary (e.g., shared gateway, caching proxy) MAY cache
  the response and serve it across authorization contexts.
- `"private"`: The response MAY be cached and reused only within the
  same authorization context. Caches MUST NOT be shared across
  authorization contexts (e.g., a different access token requires a
  different cache).

mcp_result_type.caption: MCP Result Type
mcp_result_type.description:
MCP member `resultType` (required by the protocol): Indicates the type of the result, which allows the client to determine
how to parse the result object.

Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field.
For backward compatibility, when a client receives a result from a
server implementing an earlier protocol version (which does not include
`resultType`), the client MUST treat the absent field as `"complete"`.

mcp_ttl_ms.caption: MCP Ttl Ms
mcp_ttl_ms.description:
MCP member `ttlMs` (required by the protocol): A hint from the server indicating how long (in milliseconds) the
client MAY cache this response before re-fetching. Semantics are
analogous to HTTP Cache-Control max-age.

- If 0, The response SHOULD be considered immediately stale,
  The client MAY re-fetch every time the result is needed.
- If positive, the client SHOULD consider the result fresh for this many
  milliseconds after receiving the response.

agentic_cli/mcp_model_hint.description:

Keys not declared here are currently left unspecified by the spec and are up

mcp_name.caption: MCP Name
mcp_name.description:
MCP member `name`: A hint for a model name.

The client SHOULD treat this as a substring of a model name; for example:
 - `claude-3-5-sonnet` should match `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`
 - `sonnet` should match `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`, `claude-3-sonnet-20240229`, etc.
 - `claude` should match any Claude model

The client MAY also map the string to a different provider's model name or a different model family, as long as it fills a similar niche; for example:
 - `gemini-1.5-flash` could match `claude-3-haiku-20240307`

agentic_cli/mcp_model_preferences.caption: MCP Model Preferences
agentic_cli/mcp_model_preferences.description:
The server's preferences for model selection, requested of the client during sampling.

Because LLMs can vary along multiple dimensions, choosing the "best" model is
rarely straightforward.  Different models excel in different areas—some are
faster but less capable, others are more capable but more expensive, and so
on. This interface allows servers to express their priorities across multiple
dimensions to help clients make an appropriate selection for their use case.

These preferences are always advisory. The client MAY ignore them. It is also
up to the client to decide how to interpret these preferences and how to
balance them against other considerations. Generated from the pinned MCP schema (2025-11-25 ModelPreferences; 2026-07-28 ModelPreferences).
agentic_cli/mcp_model_preferences.name: mcp_model_preferences

mcp_cost_priority.caption: MCP Cost Priority
mcp_cost_priority.description:
MCP member `costPriority`: How much to prioritize cost when selecting a model. A value of 0 means cost
is not important, while a value of 1 means cost is the most important
factor.

mcp_model_hint_list.caption: MCP Model Hint List
mcp_model_hint_list.description:
MCP member `hints`: Optional hints to use for model selection.

If multiple hints are specified, the client MUST evaluate them in order
(such that the first match is taken).

The client SHOULD prioritize these hints over the numeric priorities, but
MAY still use the priorities to select from ambiguous matches.

mcp_intelligence_priority.caption: MCP Intelligence Priority
mcp_intelligence_priority.description:
MCP member `intelligencePriority`: How much to prioritize intelligence and capabilities when selecting a
model. A value of 0 means intelligence is not important, while a value of 1
means intelligence is the most important factor.

mcp_speed_priority.caption: MCP Speed Priority
mcp_speed_priority.description:
MCP member `speedPriority`: How much to prioritize sampling speed (latency) when selecting a model. A
value of 0 means speed is not important, while a value of 1 means speed is
the most important factor.

opened the stream.

protocol_revision.caption: Protocol Revision
protocol_revision.description: The MCP protocol revision (for example 2025-11-25) only where the protocol exchange or a CLI artifact established it; never inferred from a CLI or SDK version.

1.caption: Reported in the protocol exchange
1.description: The negotiated revision of an acquired protocol message (for example an initialize result).

2.caption: Reported by a CLI artifact
2.description: A log or record the CLI wrote reports the negotiated revision for this session.

3.caption: Declared by the capture configuration
3.description: The capture declared it; not observed.

protocol_revision_basis.caption: Protocol Revision Basis
protocol_revision_basis.description: The caption of protocol_revision_basis_id, or the source's own basis for 99 Other.

target_server_name.caption: Target Server Name
target_server_name.description: The MCP server a call addresses, exactly as the source names it (usually the configured server key, which need not equal the server's self-reported name), independently of the call's reported tool_name.

1.caption: Reported members of the call
1.description: The call record names the server in a member of its own (for example server, mcpServerName).

2.caption: Reported dispatcher arguments
2.description: A dispatcher tool's reported arguments name it (for example call_mcp_tool ServerName).

3.caption: Declared derivation from an encoded tool name
3.description: Derived from the reported tool name by a pinned naming convention and confirmed unambiguous by the registered servers the source reported.

target_server_basis.caption: Target Server Basis
target_server_basis.description: The caption of target_server_basis_id, or the source's own basis for 99 Other.

target_tool_name.caption: Target Tool Name
target_tool_name.description: The MCP tool name on the addressed server, exactly as the source reports or the declared derivation yields it. The call's own tool_name and arguments are never rewritten to it.

3.caption: Declared derivation from an encoded tool name

target_tool_basis.caption: Target Tool Basis
target_tool_basis.description: The caption of target_tool_basis_id, or the source's own basis for 99 Other.

target_arguments_pointer.caption: Target Arguments Pointer
target_arguments_pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer into the event's own arguments locating the arguments the addressed tool receives (empty string: the arguments themselves; /Arguments inside a dispatcher envelope). Present only when such arguments are reported; nothing is copied.

mcp_icon_list.caption: MCP Icon List
mcp_icon_list.description:
MCP member `icons`: Optional set of sized icons that the client can display in a user interface.

Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:
- `image/png` - PNG images (safe, universal compatibility)
- `image/jpeg` (and `image/jpg`) - JPEG images (safe, universal compatibility)

Clients that support rendering icons SHOULD also support:
- `image/svg+xml` - SVG images (scalable but requires security precautions)
- `image/webp` - WebP images (modern, efficient format)

protocol_definition.caption: Protocol Definition

binding_revision.caption: Binding Revision
binding_revision.description: The pinned MCP schema revision whose binding typed the protocol object. It is the binding used, not a claim about the negotiated revision (that is protocol_revision).

projection_id.caption: Projection ID
projection_id.description: Whether a protocol object is a complete acquired protocol object, a partial projection a CLI reported, or a labelled schema example.

1.caption: Complete protocol object
1.description: The object as the protocol carried it, acquired whole.

2.caption: Partial projection
2.description: Members a CLI reported in its own records, mapped to the protocol definition; members it did not report are absent and the required ones are listed in missing_required. Nothing is synthesized to complete it.

3.caption: Schema example
3.description: A labelled synthetic or official schema example, not an observation of a run.

projection_basis.caption: Projection Basis
projection_basis.description: Which source members were mapped to which protocol members, including any renaming the CLI applied (for example structured_content as structuredContent).

missing_required.caption: Missing Required Members
missing_required.description: Protocol-required members of the definition that a partial projection does not carry.

mcp_cache_scope.caption: MCP Cache Scope
mcp_cache_scope.description:
MCP member `cacheScope` (required by the protocol): Indicates the intended scope of the cached response, analogous to HTTP
`Cache-Control: public` vs `Cache-Control: private`.

- `"public"`: The response does not contain user-specific data. Any
  client or intermediary (e.g., shared gateway, caching proxy) MAY cache
  the response and serve it across authorization contexts.
- `"private"`: The response MAY be cached and reused only within the
  same authorization context. Caches MUST NOT be shared across
  authorization contexts (e.g., a different access token requires a
  different cache).

mcp_result_type.caption: MCP Result Type
mcp_result_type.description:
MCP member `resultType` (required by the protocol): Indicates the type of the result, which allows the client to determine
how to parse the result object.

Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field.
For backward compatibility, when a client receives a result from a
server implementing an earlier protocol version (which does not include
`resultType`), the client MUST treat the absent field as `"complete"`.

mcp_ttl_ms.caption: MCP Ttl Ms
mcp_ttl_ms.description:
MCP member `ttlMs` (required by the protocol): A hint from the server indicating how long (in milliseconds) the
client MAY cache this response before re-fetching. Semantics are
analogous to HTTP Cache-Control max-age.

- If 0, The response SHOULD be considered immediately stale,
  The client MAY re-fetch every time the result is needed.
- If positive, the client SHOULD consider the result fresh for this many
  milliseconds after receiving the response.

MCP member `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`: Identifies the client software making the request. Clients SHOULD
include this field on every request unless specifically configured not
to do so.

The {@link Implementation} schema requires `name` and `version`; other
fields are optional.

The value is self-reported by the client and is not verified by the
protocol. It is intended for display, logging, and debugging. Servers
SHOULD NOT use it to change their behavior, and SHOULD NOT rely on it for
security decisions.

mcp_io_modelcontextprotocol_log_level.caption: MCP Io Modelcontextprotocol Log Level
mcp_io_modelcontextprotocol_log_level.description:
MCP member `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel`: The desired log level for this request. Optional.

If absent, the server MUST NOT send any {@link LoggingMessageNotificationnotifications/message}
notifications for this request. The client opts in to log messages by
explicitly setting a level. Replaces the former `logging/setLevel` RPC.

mcp_io_modelcontextprotocol_protocol_ver.caption: MCP Io Modelcontextprotocol Protocol Version
mcp_io_modelcontextprotocol_protocol_ver.description:
MCP member `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` (required by the protocol): The MCP Protocol Version being used for this request. Required.

For the HTTP transport, this value MUST match the `MCP-Protocol-Version`
header; otherwise the server MUST return a `400 Bad Request`. If the
server does not support the requested version, it MUST return an
{@link UnsupportedProtocolVersionError}.

agentic_cli/mcp_subscriptions_acknowledg.caption: MCP Subscriptions Acknowledged Notification
agentic_cli/mcp_subscriptions_acknowledg.description:
Sent by the server to acknowledge that a
{@link SubscriptionsListenRequestsubscriptions/listen} subscription has been
established and to report which notification types it agreed to honor.

This notification MUST be the first message the server sends carrying the
subscription's ID in `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`. The server MUST
NOT send any notification on the subscription before acknowledging it. On
stdio, where every subscription shares one channel, this ordering is defined
per subscription ID and not per channel: messages belonging to other
subscriptions MAY be interleaved before it. Generated from the pinned MCP schema (2026-07-28 SubscriptionsAcknowledgedNotification).
agentic_cli/mcp_subscriptions_acknowledg.name: mcp_subscriptions_acknowledged_notification

mcp_implementation.description:

include this field on every response unless specifically configured not
to do so.

The {@link Implementation} schema requires `name` and `version`; other
fields are optional.

protocol. It is intended for display, logging, and debugging. Clients
SHOULD NOT use it to change their behavior, and SHOULD NOT rely on it for
security decisions.

MCP member `description`: A human-readable description of the tool.

This can be used by clients to improve the LLM's understanding of available tools. It can be thought of like a "hint" to the model.

mcp_tool_execution.caption: MCP Tool Execution
mcp_tool_execution.description: MCP member `execution`: Execution-related properties for this tool.

mcp_icon_list.caption: MCP Icon List
mcp_icon_list.description:
MCP member `icons`: Optional set of sized icons that the client can display in a user interface.

Clients that support rendering icons MUST support at least the following MIME types:
- `image/png` - PNG images (safe, universal compatibility)
- `image/jpeg` (and `image/jpg`) - JPEG images (safe, universal compatibility)

Clients that support rendering icons SHOULD also support:
- `image/svg+xml` - SVG images (scalable but requires security precautions)
- `image/webp` - WebP images (modern, efficient format)

mcp_title.caption: MCP Title

even by those unfamiliar with domain-specific terminology.

If not provided, the name should be used for display (except for Tool,
where `annotations.title` should be given precedence over using `name`,
if present).

(This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)

Default: true

mcp_idempotent_hint.caption: MCP Idempotent Hint
mcp_idempotent_hint.description:
MCP member `idempotentHint`: If true, calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments
will have no additional effect on its environment.

(This property is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint == false`)

Default: false

mcp_open_world_hint.caption: MCP Open World Hint
mcp_open_world_hint.description:
MCP member `openWorldHint`: If true, this tool may interact with an "open world" of external
entities. If false, the tool's domain of interaction is closed.
For example, the world of a web search tool is open, whereas that
of a memory tool is not.

Default: true

mcp_read_only_hint.caption: MCP Read Only Hint
mcp_read_only_hint.description:
MCP member `readOnlyHint`: If true, the tool does not modify its environment.

Default: false

MCP member `content` (required by the protocol): The unstructured result content of the tool use.

This has the same format as CallToolResult.content and can include text, images,
audio, resource links, and embedded resources.

mcp_is_error.caption: MCP Is Error
mcp_is_error.description:
MCP member `isError`: Whether the tool use resulted in an error.

If true, the content typically describes the error that occurred.
Default: false

mcp_structured_content.caption: MCP Structured Content
mcp_structured_content.description:
MCP member `structuredContent`: An optional structured result object.

If the tool defined an outputSchema, this SHOULD conform to that schema.

mcp_tool_use_id.caption: MCP Tool Use Id
mcp_tool_use_id.description:
MCP member `toolUseId` (required by the protocol): The ID of the tool use this result corresponds to.

This MUST match the ID from a previous ToolUseContent.
