agentic_cli/model_ref.caption: Model Reference
agentic_cli/model_ref.description: Minimal reference to the reported model. Core ai_model requires a provider organization, which the admitted sources do not report per response; this object records provider information only with its basis.
agentic_cli/model_ref.name: model_ref

name.caption: Name
name.description: The model identifier exactly as reported.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The model version string, only when the source reports one separately from the model name.

provider_kind.caption: Provider Kind
provider_kind.description: A provider classification the source reported (for example firstParty). Not an organization name.

provider_basis_id.caption: Provider Basis ID
provider_basis_id.description: Whether provider information was reported, derived or is unavailable.

agentic_cli/observation_ref.caption: Observation Reference
agentic_cli/observation_ref.description: One source occurrence that supports a consolidated event, found in this file as a supporting observation.
agentic_cli/observation_ref.name: observation_ref

occurrence_uid.caption: Occurrence ID
occurrence_uid.description: A source occurrence: artifact, one-based record index and the emit ordinal of the event within that record (artifact#record/ordinal).

artifact.caption: Artifact
artifact.description: Name of the source artifact within the run's source inventory.

record_index.caption: Record Index
record_index.description: One-based occurrence index of the record (line) within the artifact. This is the occurrence identity; native ids may repeat or be absent.

emit_ordinal.caption: Emit Ordinal
emit_ordinal.description: The zero-based position of an event among the events its mapper emitted for one native record.

agentic_cli/operation.caption: Operation
agentic_cli/operation.description: A separately reported operation with its own identity and observed outcome. Its attribution states whether the source establishes a wrapping tool call: an operation the source reports on its own is a standalone observation, attributed Unattributed at its reported scope, never given an invented owner.
agentic_cli/operation.name: operation

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The operation's native identifier.

identity_basis_id.caption: Identity Basis ID
identity_basis_id.description: What kind of identifier the source reported as this fact's identity: tool_call_uid on a tool_call event, uid on an operation, item_uid on a model_response. A stream-local item identifier is not the identifier the model used for the call or the provider's response identifier, and cannot be joined with one.

1.caption: Model-facing call identifier
1.description: The identifier the model's own tool request carried, as the source reports it.

2.caption: Stream-local item identifier
2.description: An identifier the CLI's output stream assigns to its own items. It is unique only within one source artifact of one Journal invocation (journal.run_uid, journal.invocation_index, source_ref.artifact): an equal value in another invocation is another item. The model-facing call or response identifier is not reported.

argv.caption: Command Vector
argv.description: The command as an argument vector when the source reports it that way.

command_line.caption: Command Line
command_line.description: The command exactly as the source reported it, as one string. Never parsed into argv; a shell's interpretation of it is not reported by this attribute.

exit_code.caption: Exit Code
exit_code.description: The exit code reported by a process when it terminates. The convention is that zero indicates success and any non-zero exit code indicates that some error occurred.

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example DONE, completed, failed).

attribution.caption: Attribution
attribution.description: How this fact was associated with its owner, with the declared outcome, candidates and basis.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native operation record exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/permission_decision.caption: Permission Decision
agentic_cli/permission_decision.description: A permission decision at its reported scope. A decision reported without a reference to a tool call is retained at run or turn scope with an unattributed or ambiguous attribution; it is never attached to a tool call by guess.
agentic_cli/permission_decision.name: permission_decision

decision_id.caption: Decision ID
decision_id.description: Normalized permission decision. The core sibling decision carries the caption; reported_decision carries the source's own label.

decision.caption: Authorization Decision/Outcome
decision.description: Decision/outcome of the authorization mechanism (e.g. Approved, Denied)

reported_decision.caption: Reported Decision
reported_decision.description: The source's own decision label exactly as reported (for example accept, denied). decision carries the normalized caption.

decision_source.caption: Decision Source
decision_source.description: Who or what made the decision, as reported (for example config, user, cli).

reason_type.caption: Reason Type
reason_type.description: The reason category reported with the decision.

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation. 99 Other names, in its sibling scope, a unit the source defines that no other value describes.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A unit the source itself defines, which none of the other scopes describes; the sibling scope names it (for example Conversation step). It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation).

scope.caption: Scope
scope.description: Caption sibling of scope_id; for 99 Other, the name of the source-defined unit.

attribution.caption: Attribution
attribution.description: How this fact was associated with its owner, with the declared outcome, candidates and basis.

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native decision record exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/session_settings.caption: Session Settings
agentic_cli/session_settings.description: Launch/session settings as one native record reports them. Every attribute is optional: only reported values are present; nothing is defaulted or inferred.
agentic_cli/session_settings.name: session_settings

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: The working directory the CLI reported.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model identifier the CLI reported as configured.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The model provider the CLI reported (a reported string, not an inferred organization).

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CLI version the record itself reports.

permission_mode.caption: Permission Mode
permission_mode.description: The CLI's reported permission/approval mode string exactly as reported (for example default, acceptEdits).

approval_policy.caption: Approval Policy
approval_policy.description: The CLI's reported approval policy string exactly as reported (for example never, on-request).

sandbox_policy.caption: Sandbox Policy
sandbox_policy.description: The CLI's reported sandbox policy exactly as reported (string or object).

tool_names.caption: Tool Names
tool_names.description: The tool names the CLI reported as available, in reported order.

git_branch.caption: Git Branch
git_branch.description: The git branch the CLI reported for the working directory.

agentic_cli/source_ref.caption: Source Reference
agentic_cli/source_ref.description: Identifies the native artifact and record occurrence that supplied a fact. The artifact hash is stored once per run in run.json sources and reached through artifact; it appears here only in a self-contained export.
agentic_cli/source_ref.name: source_ref

source_kind_id.caption: Source Kind ID
source_kind_id.description: What kind of artifact supplied the fact: the CLI's live output (standard output or standard error), a native session file it saved, a telemetry export it wrote (native OTel), a report file it wrote at exit, or its own log file.

3.caption: Telemetry export
3.description: A telemetry file the CLI's own exporter wrote during the run (for example the OTel file exporter).

4.caption: CLI report file
4.description: A report the CLI wrote at the end of the run (for example a usage report file).

5.caption: CLI log file
5.description: The CLI's own diagnostic log, or a declared excerpt of it.

artifact.caption: Artifact
artifact.description: Name of the source artifact within the run's source inventory.

artifact_sha256.caption: Artifact SHA-256
artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the complete source artifact bytes.

record_index.caption: Record Index
record_index.description: One-based occurrence index of the record (line) within the artifact. This is the occurrence identity; native ids may repeat or be absent.

native_uid.caption: Native Record ID
native_uid.description: The record's own identifier when the source reports one.

native_time.caption: Native Time Text
native_time.description: The record's timestamp text verbatim, when reported.

record_bytes.caption: Record Bytes
record_bytes.description: Byte length of the record line excluding the line terminator.

line_ending.caption: Line Ending
line_ending.description: The line terminator observed after the record: LF, CRLF or none (last line without terminator).

is_whole_record.caption: Is Whole Record
is_whole_record.description: True when the event's data attribute holds the complete native record; false when it holds a fragment (for example one block). Reconstruction uses whole-record events only.

agentic_cli/tool_definition.caption: Tool Definition
agentic_cli/tool_definition.description: A tool the CLI or a server declared as available, in any declaration format (an MCP Tool, a function declaration, a vendor tool record): its name, description, input and output JSON Schemas and annotations as reported. A source that reports only a name or a hash of the schema states only that; a hash is never the schema.
agentic_cli/tool_definition.name: tool_definition

name.caption: Name
name.description: The tool name exactly as declared.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A human-readable title the declaration gives the tool, exactly as declared.

tool_description.caption: Tool Description
tool_description.description: A tool's description exactly as declared.

input_schema.caption: Input Schema
input_schema.description: The JSON Schema a tool declares for its input, exactly as reported.

output_schema.caption: Output Schema
output_schema.description: The JSON Schema a tool declares for its structured output, exactly as reported.

definition_format_id.caption: Definition Format ID
definition_format_id.description: The declaration format of a tool definition.

1.caption: MCP Tool
1.description: An MCP Tool definition (typed in mcp).

2.caption: Function declaration
2.description: A function-calling declaration (type function, name, description, parameters), as OpenAI-compatible APIs and OTel gen_ai.tool.definitions carry it.

3.caption: Name and schema hash
3.description: Only the tool name and a hash of its schema; the schema itself is not reported.

4.caption: Name only
4.description: Only the tool name.

schema_hash.caption: Schema Hash
schema_hash.description: A hash of a tool's schema exactly as the source reported it; it identifies, it does not contain, the schema.

mcp.caption: MCP Observation
mcp.description: What this event observed of a Model Context Protocol interaction: protocol revision and basis, the addressed server and tool with their bases, and typed protocol objects (complete, partial CLI projection or schema example).

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native declaration exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/tool_result.caption: Tool Result
agentic_cli/tool_result.description: The result returned for a tool call as the source reported it.
agentic_cli/tool_result.name: tool_result

data.caption: Data
data.description: The model-visible result content exactly as reported (string, array or object).

error_reported.caption: Error Reported
error_reported.description: Whether the source explicitly flagged the result as an error. Absent when the source reports nothing.

structured_result.caption: Structured Result
structured_result.description: Structured result detail the CLI reported beside the model-visible content (for example Claude's tool_use_result).

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example DONE, completed, failed).

errors.caption: Errors
errors.description: Each error reported for this result with the layer that reported it (JSON-RPC, tool result, CLI, capture).

agentic_cli/usage_component.caption: Usage Component
agentic_cli/usage_component.description: How one canonical usage component of an observation was established: reported (copied from one native member), derived exactly by a declared rule from named native members, or unavailable from what the source reported; and, where a declared rule establishes it, what the source establishes about the component's quantity (measured, possibly the source's default, at least the stated value, or, for an unavailable component, a conditional formula result kept apart from the canonical value).
agentic_cli/usage_component.name: usage_component

name.caption: Name
name.description: The canonical component attribute, for example uncached_input_tokens.

component_basis_id.caption: Component Basis ID
component_basis_id.description: How a canonical usage component was established.

1.caption: Reported
1.description: Copied exactly from the one native member named.

2.caption: Derived
2.description: Computed exactly from the native members named, by the declared rule in derivation, whose arithmetic the source establishes.

3.caption: Unavailable
3.description: The source reports related members, but they do not establish this component (derivation states why); the component is absent, never zero.

measurement_status_id.caption: Measurement Status ID
measurement_status_id.description: What the source establishes about this component's quantity, apart from component_basis_id; absent when no declared rule states it.

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source establishes this exact value as a measurement of the quantity; for a running total, of every contribution to it.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

3.caption: Conditional
3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.

conditional_value.caption: Conditional Value
conditional_value.description: With measurement_status_id 3 Conditional: the declared formula's result, which is this component's quantity only under the assumptions the derivation names; the canonical component value stays absent.

native_pointers.caption: Native Pointers
native_pointers.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointers into the observation's data naming the native members a value was copied or derived from.

derivation.caption: Derivation
derivation.description: The declared rule and its arithmetic for a derived component; for a conditional value, the formula and every assumption it needs; why the component is unavailable otherwise.

agentic_cli/usage_observation.caption: Usage Observation
agentic_cli/usage_observation.description: One reported token-usage observation, in disjoint economic tranches: uncached input, cache reads and cache writes (with their tiers), and output with its reasoning part. Scope, aggregation and finality are separate facets; components are present only when reported or exactly derived (components[] says which); absence is not zero. data keeps the native usage object exactly.
agentic_cli/usage_observation.name: usage_observation

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation. At 99 Other the unit, named in scope, is the enclosing event's own item: its item_uid (or tool_call_uid) in the namespace that event's identity_basis_id states, within the observation's source artifact.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A unit the source itself defines, which none of the other scopes describes; the sibling scope names it (for example Conversation step). It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation).

scope.caption: Scope
scope.description: Caption sibling of scope_id; for 99 Other, the name of the source-defined unit.

usage_status_id.caption: Usage Status ID
usage_status_id.description: Whether the reported usage is provisional or final, as established by the declared rule in basis.

aggregation_id.caption: Aggregation ID
aggregation_id.description: How the observation's components accumulate, independently of its scope (scope_id) and finality (usage_status_id).

1.caption: Scope total
1.description: The consumption of exactly the observation's scope unit (for example one model response); observations of distinct units of that scope are disjoint.

2.caption: Cumulative snapshot
2.description: A running total of the scope unit from its start up to the point of observation. It may include consumption before this capture began and is not the unit's completed total; two snapshots of one unit overlap and are never summed.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rules that established usage_status_id and aggregation_id.

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

model_ref.caption: Model Reference
model_ref.description: Minimal reported-model reference. Used instead of core ai_model when the source does not report a provider organization.

uncached_input_tokens.caption: Uncached Input Tokens
uncached_input_tokens.description: Ordinary input tokens: input neither read from nor written to a prompt cache. Disjoint from cache_read_tokens and cache_write_tokens. Present only when the source reports this component or a declared rule derives it exactly from components whose arithmetic the source establishes (components[] names which); otherwise absent and, when the source's components cannot establish it, listed as unavailable. A formula result that is this quantity only under named assumptions is never this value; it is the component's conditional_value. Replaces input_tokens of 0.5.0-prototype and earlier, whose meaning followed each vendor.

cache_read_tokens.caption: Cache Read Tokens
cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from a prompt cache. Disjoint from uncached_input_tokens and cache_write_tokens.

cache_write_tokens.caption: Cache Write Tokens
cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to a prompt cache, every retention or pricing tier together. Disjoint from uncached_input_tokens and cache_read_tokens; cache_write_tiers breaks it down without adding to it.

cache_write_tiers.caption: Cache Write Tiers
cache_write_tiers.description: The source-reported breakdown of cache_write_tokens by retention or pricing tier. Each tier's count is a part of cache_write_tokens, never additional usage.

output_tokens.caption: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Output tokens as the source reports them. When reasoning_relation_id is 1, reasoning_tokens are part of this count, never in addition to it.

reasoning_tokens.caption: Reasoning Tokens
reasoning_tokens.description: Reasoning or thinking output tokens as the source reports them. reasoning_relation_id states whether they are part of output_tokens; absent there, the relation is not established and they must not be added to or subtracted from output_tokens.

reasoning_relation_id.caption: Reasoning Relation ID
reasoning_relation_id.description: Whether reasoning_tokens are part of output_tokens, as the source's own arithmetic establishes. Absent when no declared rule establishes it.

1.caption: Part of output
1.description: reasoning_tokens are a subset of output_tokens: never another additive count or charge.

2.caption: Separate from output
2.description: reasoning_tokens are not counted in output_tokens.

reported_total_tokens.caption: Reported Total Tokens
reported_total_tokens.description: A total token figure only when the source reported it as a total. Never computed.

components.caption: Components
components.description: For each canonical usage component this observation states or cannot state: whether its value was copied from a reported native member, derived by a declared rule from named native members, or is unavailable from what the source reported. The native values themselves stay in data.

measurement_status_id.caption: Measurement Status ID
measurement_status_id.description: What the source establishes about the reported quantity: of the whole usage observation, or (on a usage component) of that one component's canonical quantity. Separate from how Journal obtained a component (component_basis_id). Absent when no declared rule states it.

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source establishes this exact value as a measurement of the quantity; for a running total, of every contribution to it.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

3.caption: Conditional
3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native usage object exactly as reported.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: An autonomous AI agent that performs tasks under delegated authority. Distinguished from the OCSF agent object (which describes security sensors such as EDR and DLP tools) and from human principals. An AI agent has a stable logical identity across runs and a restart-sensitive instance identity. The agent owns its model; the ai_model attribute captures which model was backing the agent at the time of action.
ai_agent.name: ai_agent

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable name for the agent. For example: Q4 Analysis Agent or Model Tester Agent.

uid.caption: AI Agent ID
uid.description: The stable logical identifier for the agent, assigned by the agent's authoritative source (e.g., its control plane, registry, or issuing identity provider). Persists across restarts and instances. Producers populate this from whatever identity they observe: for a runtime that owns the agent, this is its issued ID; for a gateway or proxy, it is typically derived from the agent's credential. Multiple producers logging the same agent should converge on the same uid when they share an authoritative source.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model backing this agent at the time of the recorded event. An agent's model may change across instances or versions; this captures the model in use for the specific logged activity or delegation.

charter.caption: Agent Charter
charter.description: A document that defines an AI agent's durable role, responsibilities, constraints, and operating boundaries. When available, populate hashes on the file for content integrity and signatures for provenance. Integrity of the event that reports this agent is provided separately by the record_integrity profile.

instance_uid.caption: AI Agent Instance ID
instance_uid.description: Identifier for a specific running instance or session of the agent, distinct from the stable logical uid. An instance is a single materialization of the agent: a conversation, session, or run. It may persist across restarts (a session that is suspended and later resumed keeps the same instance_uid) and may span multiple cooperating runtime components, so several events can share one instance_uid. Enables attribution of actions to a particular instance of the agent rather than to the agent generally.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The agent framework, normalized to the caption of the type_id value.

type_id.caption: Agent Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the agent framework. Different agent frameworks have different identity, tool-call, and delegation semantics, so recording the framework enables cross-framework normalization. Communication protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) are a property of individual operations rather than the agent itself, and are surfaced on the relevant operation rather than here.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The agent framework is not listed. Use the type attribute to describe it.

1.caption: Native
1.description: A first-party or proprietary agent built without a third-party agent framework. For example, a custom orchestrator or an LLM provider's own agent SDK.

2.caption: LangChain
2.description: An agent built with the LangChain framework.

3.caption: AutoGen
3.description: An agent built with the AutoGen framework for multi-agent conversation and orchestration.

4.caption: CrewAI
4.description: An agent built with the CrewAI framework for role-based multi-agent collaboration.

version.caption: AI Agent Version
version.description: The version of the agent: the agent's own code or configuration revision (e.g., 1.4.2), distinct from the version of the model backing it (carried on ai_model.version). Enables correlation of behavioral changes with charter or configuration revisions across agent versions.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI Model object describes the characteristics of an AI/ML model. Examples include language models like GPT-4, embedding models like text-embedding-ada-002, and computer vision models like CLIP.
ai_model.name: ai_model

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable model name. For example: gpt-4o, claude-3-sonnet, or text-embedding-ada-002.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the AI model.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_provider.caption: AI Provider
ai_provider.description: AI service provider or organization name. For example: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Internal.

version.caption: Version
version.description: Model version identifier. For example: 2024-05-13, v2.1.0, or beta.

references.description: AI Model Registry and Documentation Standards

analytic.description: The Analytic object contains details about the analytic technique used to analyze and derive insights from the data or information that led to the creation of a finding or conclusion.

name.description: The name of the analytic that generated the finding.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the analytic that generated the finding.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.

algorithm.description: The algorithm used by the underlying analytic to generate the finding.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the analytic that generated the finding.

related_analytics.caption: Related Analytics
related_analytics.description: Other analytics related to this analytic.

@deprecated.message: Related Analytics has been decoupled from this object, instead use finding_info.related_analytics.

sensor_info_list.caption: Sensor Information List
sensor_info_list.description: An array of sensor_info objects, each describing a sensor control point analyzed or correlated by the analytic. Each element typically represents a source of related_events that contributed to the finding. An individual sensor control point may also directly originate the finding, though more commonly it emits alerts that a downstream consumer treats as findings.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The state is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Active
1.description: The Analytic is active.

2.caption: Suppressed
2.description: The Analytic is suppressed. For example, a user/customer has suppressed a particular detection signature in a security product.

3.caption: Experimental
3.description: The Analytic is still under development and considered experimental.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The analytic type.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Rule
1.description: A Rule in security analytics refers to predefined criteria or conditions set to monitor, alert, or enforce policies, playing a crucial role in access control, threat detection, and regulatory compliance across security systems.

2.caption: Behavioral
2.description: Behavioral analytics focus on monitoring and analyzing user or system actions to identify deviations from established patterns, aiding in the detection of insider threats, fraud, and advanced persistent threats (APTs).

3.caption: Statistical
3.description: Statistical analytics pertains to analyzing data patterns and anomalies using statistical models to predict, detect, and respond to potential threats, enhancing overall security posture through informed decision-making.

4.caption: Learning (ML/DL)
4.description: Learning (ML/DL) encompasses techniques that can "learn" from known data to create analytics that generalize to new data. There may be a statistical component to these techniques, but it is not a requirement.

5.caption: Fingerprinting
5.description: Fingerprinting is the technique of collecting detailed system data, including software versions and configurations, to enhance threat detection, data loss prevention (DLP), and endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities.

6.caption: Tagging
6.description: Tagging refers to the practice of assigning labels or identifiers to data, users, assets, or activities to monitor, control access, and facilitate incident response across various security domains such as DLP and EDR.

7.caption: Keyword Match
7.description: Keyword Match involves scanning content for specific terms to identify sensitive information, potential threats, or policy violations, aiding in DLP and compliance monitoring.

8.caption: Regular Expressions
8.description: Regular Expressions are used to define complex search patterns for identifying, validating, and extracting specific data sets or threats within digital content, enhancing DLP, EDR, and threat detection mechanisms.

9.caption: Exact Data Match
9.description: Exact Data Match is a precise comparison technique used to detect the unauthorized use or exposure of specific, sensitive information, crucial for enforcing DLP policies and protecting against data breaches.

10.caption: Partial Data Match
10.description: Partial Data Match involves identifying instances where segments of sensitive information or patterns match, facilitating nuanced DLP and threat detection without requiring complete data conformity.

11.caption: Indexed Data Match
11.description: Indexed Data Match refers to comparing content against a pre-compiled index of sensitive information to efficiently detect and prevent unauthorized access or breaches, streamlining DLP and compliance efforts.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The analytic version. For example: 1.1.

api.caption: API
api.description: The API, or Application Programming Interface, object represents  information pertaining to an API request and response.
api.name: api

group.caption: Group
group.description: The information pertaining to the API group.

request.caption: API Request Details
request.description: Details pertaining to the API request.

response.caption: API Response Details
response.description: Details pertaining to the API response.

service.caption: Service
service.description: The information pertaining to the API service.

token.caption: Token
token.description: The API or client token used to authenticate or authorize the API request. This attribute contains the base token object that represents: (1) IdP-issued client tokens (type_id: 6) such as Okta API tokens or Microsoft Entra ID Application Registration client secrets, or (2) generic API tokens/keys (type_id: 7) used for SaaS application authentication. Use this attribute when the API request was authenticated using a token that should be tracked as part of the API activity event. Note: Protocol-specific authentication tokens (Kerberos, OIDC, SAML) should be represented using authentication_token in authentication events, not in API activity events.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the API service.

application.caption: Application
application.description: An Application describes the details for an inventoried application as reported by an Application Security tool or other Developer-centric tooling. Applications can be defined as Kubernetes resources, Containerized resources, or application hosting-specific cloud sources such as AWS Elastic BeanStalk, AWS Lightsail, or Azure Logic Apps.
application.name: application

criticality.caption: Business Criticality
criticality.description: The criticality of the application as defined by the event source.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Additional data describing the application.

desc.caption: Application Description
desc.description: A description or commentary for an application, usually retrieved from an upstream system.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The name of the related application or associated resource group.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the application.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the application.

name.caption: Application Name
name.description: The name of the application.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the application.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The software product that this application is an instance of, carrying product identity such as vendor_name, cpe_name, and canonical version.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The cloud region of the resource.

resource_relationship.caption: Application Relationship
resource_relationship.description: A graph representation showing how this application relates to and interacts with other entities in the environment. This can include parent/child relationships, dependencies, or other connections.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

sbom.caption: Related SBOM
sbom.description: The Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) associated with the application

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the application.

type.caption: Application Type
type.description: The type of application as defined by the event source, e.g., GitHub, Azure Logic App, or Amazon Elastic BeanStalk.

uid.caption: Application ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the application.

uid_alt.caption: Application Alternative ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the application, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

version.caption: Application Version
version.description: The semantic version of the application, e.g., 1.7.4.

attack.caption: Attack Tactics & Techniques
attack.description: The Attack object describes the tactic, technique, sub-technique & mitigation associated to an attack.
attack.name: attack

mitigation.caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.description: The Mitigation object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.

sub_technique.caption: MITRE Sub-technique
sub_technique.description: The Sub-technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Sub-technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactic.caption: MITRE Tactic
tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the Tactic ID and/or name associated to an attack.

tactics.caption: Tactics
tactics.description: The Tactics associated with the attack technique.

technique.caption: MITRE Technique
technique.description: The Technique object describes the MITRE ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Technique ID and/or name associated to an attack.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Matrix version.

attestation.caption: Attestation
attestation.description: A cryptographic attestation that an event has not been altered since it was produced and was produced by the holder of a verifiable identity, providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. The attestation is computed over a canonical serialization of the event: the entire event, including the attestation's own authority_uid, chain_uid, and prev_event attributes, and excluding only the attestation's fingerprint and signatures. Because prev_event is inside the serialized content, deleting or altering an event in a chain breaks the fingerprint and signatures of the event that references it. An attestation may carry more than one signature (for example, a co-signature, notary, or witness over the same event). The verifiable identity is a technical credential, such as a key or certificate, and is not an attribution of any person, organization, or state.
attestation.name: attestation

authority_uid.caption: Authority ID
authority_uid.description: Unique identifier of the authority that produced this attestation. When the attestation has a signature, authority_uid ties the signing credential to a known party: because signing credentials rotate and expire, a verifier uses this identifier to confirm that the credential belongs to the expected authority, rather than to a different holder of some otherwise-valid credential. Where multiple signatures are present, it identifies the authority that produced the attestation; the identity of each co-signer is carried within its own digital_signature object. Included in the canonical serialization.

chain_uid.caption: Chain ID
chain_uid.description: Identifier of the append-only chain, such as a forensic or audit log, that this event belongs to. It groups a sequence of attestations so that an independent verifier can locate and validate them in order; it identifies the chain itself and is not a reference to any event outside of this one. Stable for the lifetime of the chain. For example, every attestation produced during a single agent session shares one chain_uid, so querying events whose attestation.chain_uid matches retrieves the full chain, including its newest entry, while each event links to its predecessor through prev_event.

fingerprint.caption: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of this event's canonical serialization. If signatures are present, each signature is computed over this fingerprint. Without signatures, the fingerprint alone still detects accidental alteration or corruption of the event. The next event in a chain references this value through its own prev_event.fingerprint.

prev_event.caption: Previous Event
prev_event.description: Reference to the previous event in a tamper-evident chain, carrying that event's fingerprint together with locator attributes for retrieval. Absent on the first, or genesis, event of a chain.

signatures.caption: Digital Signatures
signatures.description: One or more digital signatures, each computed over this event's fingerprint and thereby over the event's canonical serialization, each bound to a verifiable identity. The first entry is typically the producer; additional entries carry co-signatures such as a notary or witness over the same event. The signing algorithm, certificate or public-key material, and signing time are carried within each digital_signature object.

uid.caption: Attestation ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of this attestation. It distinguishes an individual attestation, such as a single entry within a tamper-evident chain, from the chain as a whole. See chain_uid for the identifier of the chain itself.

auth_factor.caption: Authentication Factor
auth_factor.description: An Authentication Factor object describes a category of methods used for identity verification in an authentication attempt.
auth_factor.name: auth_factor

device.caption: Device
device.description: Device used to complete an authentication request.

email_addr.caption: Email Address
email_addr.description: The email address used in an email-based authentication factor.

factor_type.caption: Factor Type
factor_type.description: The type of authentication factor used in an authentication attempt.

factor_type_id.caption: Factor Type ID
factor_type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the authentication factor.

1.caption: SMS
1.description: User receives and inputs a code sent to their mobile device via SMS text message.

2.caption: Security Question
2.description: The user responds to a security question as part of a question-based authentication factor

3.caption: Phone Call
3.description: System calls the user's registered phone number and requires the user to answer and provide a response.

4.caption: Biometric
4.description: Devices that verify identity-based on user's physical identifiers, such as fingerprint scanners or retina scanners.

5.caption: Push Notification
5.description: Push notification is sent to user's registered device and requires the user to acknowledge.

6.caption: Hardware Token
6.description: Physical device that generates a code to be used for authentication.

7.caption: OTP
7.description: Application generates a one-time password (OTP) for use in authentication.

8.caption: Email
8.description: A code or link is sent to a user's registered email address.

9.caption: U2F
9.description: Typically involves a hardware token, which the user physically interacts with to authenticate.

10.caption: WebAuthn
10.description: Web-based API that enables users to register devices as authentication factors.

11.caption: Password
11.description: The user enters a password that they have previously established.

is_hotp.caption: HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP)
is_hotp.description: Whether the authentication factor is an HMAC-based One-time Password (HOTP).

is_totp.caption: Time-based One-time Password (TOTP)

security_questions.caption: Security Questions

authorization.caption: Authorization Result

policy.caption: Policy

cis_control.caption: CIS Control
cis_control.description: The CIS Control (aka Critical Security Control) object describes a prioritized set of actions to protect your organization and data from cyber-attack vectors. The CIS Controls are defined by the Center for Internet Security.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: The Classifier Details object describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: The Cloud object describes the cloud computing environment where an event or finding originated. It provides comprehensive context about the cloud infrastructure, including the cloud service provider, account or subscription details, organizational structure, geographic regions, availability zones, and logical partitions.
cloud.name: cloud

account.caption: Account
account.description:
The Account object containing details about the cloud account, subscription, or billing unit where the event or finding was created. This object includes properties such as the account name, unique identifier, type, labels, and tags.

Examples:
  • AWS: Account object with name, uid (Account ID), type, and other account properties
  • Azure: Subscription object with name, uid (Subscription ID), type, and subscription metadata
  • GCP: Project object with name, uid (Project ID), type, and project attributes
  • Oracle Cloud: Compartment object with name, uid (Tenancy OCID), type, and compartment details

cloud_partition.caption: Cloud Partition
cloud_partition.description:
The logical grouping or isolated segment within a cloud provider's infrastructure where the event or finding was created, often used for compliance, governance, or regional separation.

Examples:
  • AWS: Partition where the event occurred (aws, aws-cn, aws-us-gov)
  • Azure: Cloud environment where the event occurred (AzureCloud, AzureUSGovernment, AzureChinaCloud)

org.caption: Organization
org.description:
The Organization object containing details about the organizational unit or management structure that governs the account, subscription, or project where the event or finding was created. This object includes properties such as the organization name, unique identifier, type, and other organizational metadata.

Examples:
  • AWS: Organization object with name, uid (Organization ID), type, and other organizational properties
  • Azure: Management Group object with name, uid (Management Group ID), type, and management group metadata
  • GCP: Organization object with name, uid (Organization ID), type, and organizational attributes
  • Oracle Cloud: Tenancy object with name, uid (Tenancy OCID), type, and tenancy details

project_uid.caption: Project ID
project_uid.description: The unique identifier of a Cloud project.

provider.caption: Cloud Provider
provider.description: The unique name of the Cloud services provider where the event or finding was created. Examples include AWS, Azure, GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, or other public, private, or hybrid cloud providers.

region.caption: Region
region.description:
The cloud region where the event or finding was created, as defined by the cloud provider.

Examples:
  • AWS: Region where the event occurred (us-east-1, eu-west-1)
  • Azure: Region where the event occurred (East US, West Europe)
  • GCP: Region where the event occurred (us-central1, europe-west1)
  • Oracle Cloud: Region where the event occurred (us-ashburn-1, uk-london-1)

zone.caption: Cloud Availability Zone
zone.description:
The availability zone in the cloud region where the event or finding was created, as defined by the cloud provider.

Examples:
  • AWS: Availability zone where the event occurred (us-east-1a, us-east-1b)
  • Azure: Availability zone where the event occurred (1, 2, 3 within a region)
  • GCP: Availability zone where the event occurred (us-central1-a, us-central1-b)
  • Oracle Cloud: Availability zone where the event occurred (AD-1, AD-2, AD-3)

container.caption: Container
container.description: The Container object describes an instance of a specific container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.
container.name: container

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Commit hash of image created for docker or the SHA256 hash of the container. For example: 13550340a8681c84c861aac2e5b440161c2b33a3e4f302ac680ca5b686de48de.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The container image used as a template to run the container.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the container.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The container name.

network_driver.caption: Network Driver
network_driver.description: The network driver used by the container. For example, bridge, overlay, host, none, etc.

orchestrator.caption: Orchestrator
orchestrator.description: The orchestrator managing the container, such as ECS, EKS, K8s, or OpenShift.

pod_uuid.caption: Pod UUID
pod_uuid.description: The unique identifier of the pod (or equivalent) that the container is executing on.

runtime.caption: Runtime
runtime.description: The backend running the container, such as containerd or cri-o.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size of the container image.

tag.caption: Image Tag
tag.description: The tag used by the container. It can indicate version, format, OS.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the container.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The full container unique identifier for this instantiation of the container. For example: ac2ea168264a08f9aaca0dfc82ff3551418dfd22d02b713142a6843caa2f61bf.

cpu_info.caption: CPU Information
cpu_info.description: The CPU information object contains attributes describing a physical CPU package installed in the device.
cpu_info.name: cpu_info

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

cpu_architecture.caption: CPU Architecture
cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

cpu_architecture_id.caption: CPU Architecture ID
cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

1.caption: x86
1.description: CPU uses the x86 ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

2.caption: ARM
2.description: CPU uses the ARM ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

3.caption: RISC-V
3.description: CPU uses the RISC-V ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The CPU architecture is not mapped. See the cpu_architecture attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The number of bits used by the CPU for memory addressing.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the CPU. For example: Intel Xeon Gold 6348, AMD EPYC 7763, or Apple M3 Max.

speed_mhz.caption: Compute Unit Speed (MHz)
speed_mhz.description: The nominal clock speed of the unit, expressed in megahertz.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the CPU. For example: Intel, AMD, or Apple.

cve.caption: CVE
cve.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) object represents publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities defined in CVE Program catalog (CVE). There is one CVE Record for each vulnerability in the catalog.
cve.name: cve

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The CVSS object details Common Vulnerability Scoring System scores from the advisory that are related to the vulnerability.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.

cwe_uid.caption: CWE UID
cwe_uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) unique identifier. For example: CWE-787.

cwe_url.caption: CWE URL
cwe_url.description: Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) definition URL. For example: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/787.html.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the CVE Record.

epss.caption: EPSS
epss.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) object describes the estimated probability a vulnerability will be exploited. EPSS is a community-driven effort to combine descriptive information about vulnerabilities (CVEs) with evidence of actual exploitation in-the-wild.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the CVE Record.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: Describes the Common Weakness Enumeration details related to the CVE Record.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the CVE record.

type.caption: Vulnerability Type
type.description:
The vulnerability type as classified in the CVE catalog.

Most frequently used vulnerability types are: DoS, Code Execution, Overflow, Memory Corruption, Sql Injection, XSS, Directory Traversal, Http Response Splitting, Bypass something, Gain Information, Gain Privileges, CSRF, File Inclusion. For more information see Vulnerabilities By Type distributions.

uid.caption: CVE ID
uid.description: The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures unique number assigned to a specific computer vulnerability. A CVE Identifier begins with 4 digits representing the year followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CVE-2021-12345.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The Record Creation Date identifies when the CVE ID was issued to a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) or the CVE Record was published on the CVE List. Note that the Record Creation Date does not necessarily indicate when this vulnerability was discovered, shared with the affected vendor, publicly disclosed, or updated in CVE.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The Record Modified Date identifies when the CVE record was last updated.

cvss.caption: CVSS Score
cvss.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) object provides a way to capture the principal characteristics of a vulnerability and produce a numerical score reflecting its severity.
cvss.name: cvss

base_score.caption: Base Score
base_score.description: The CVSS base score. For example: 9.1.

depth.caption: CVSS Depth
depth.description: The CVSS depth represents a depth of the equation used to calculate CVSS score.

metrics.caption: Metrics
metrics.description: The Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. This attribute contains information on the CVE's impact. If the CVE has been analyzed, this attribute will contain any CVSSv2 or CVSSv3 information associated with the vulnerability. For example: { {"Access Vector", "Network"}, {"Access Complexity", "Low"}, ...}.

overall_score.caption: Overall Score
overall_score.description: The CVSS overall score, impacted by base, temporal, and environmental metrics. For example: 9.1.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description:
The Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Qualitative Severity Rating. A textual representation of the numeric score.

CVSS v2.0
  • Low (0.0 – 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 – 6.9)
  • High (7.0 – 10.0)

CVSS v3.0
  • None (0.0)
  • Low (0.1 - 3.9)
  • Medium (4.0 - 6.9)
  • High (7.0 - 8.9)
  • Critical (9.0 - 10.0)

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL for the CVSS score. For example: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228

vector_string.caption: Vector String
vector_string.description: The CVSS vector string is a text representation of a set of CVSS metrics. It is commonly used to record or transfer CVSS metric information in a concise form. For example: 3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor that provided the CVSS score. For example: NVD, REDHAT etc.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CVSS version. For example: 3.1.

cwe.caption: CWE
cwe.description: The CWE object represents a weakness in a software system that can be exploited by a threat actor to perform an attack. The CWE object is based on the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog.
cwe.name: cwe

caption.caption: Caption
caption.description: The caption assigned to the Common Weakness Enumeration unique identifier.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: URL pointing to the CWE Specification. For more information see CWE.

uid.caption: CWE ID
uid.description: The Common Weakness Enumeration unique number assigned to a specific weakness. A CWE Identifier begins "CWE" followed by a sequence of digits that acts as a unique identifier. For example: CWE-123.

d3f_tactic.caption: Defensive Tactic
d3f_tactic.description: The Defensive Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.
d3f_tactic.name: d3f_tactic

name.caption: Name
name.description: The tactic name that is associated with the defensive technique. For example: Isolate.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive tactic.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive tactic. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/tactic/d3f:Isolate/

d3f_technique.caption: Defensive Technique
d3f_technique.description: The Defensive Technique object describes the leaf defensive technique ID and/or name associated to a countermeasure.
d3f_technique.name: d3f_technique

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the defensive technique. For example: IO Port Restriction.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the defensive technique. For example: D3-IOPR.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the defensive technique. For example: https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:IOPortRestriction/

d3fend.caption: Defensive Countermeasure
d3fend.description: The Defensive Countermeasure object describes the tactic & technique associated with a countermeasure.
d3fend.name: d3fend

d3f_tactic.caption: MITRE D3FEND™ Tactic
d3f_tactic.description: The Tactic object describes the tactic ID and/or name that is associated with a countermeasure.

d3f_technique.caption: MITRE D3FEND™ Technique
d3f_technique.description: The Technique object describes the technique ID and/or name associated with a countermeasure.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The D3FEND™ Matrix version.

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.
data_classification.name: data_classification

category.caption: Category
category.description: The name of the data classification category that data matched into, e.g. Financial, Personal, Governmental, etc.

category_id.caption: Category ID
category_id.description: The normalized identifier of the data classification category.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The type is not mapped. See the data_type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Personal
1.description: Any Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Electronic Personal Health Information (ePHI), or similarly personal information. E.g., full name, home address, date of birth, etc.

2.caption: Governmental
2.description: Any sensitive government identification number related to a person or other classified material. E.g., Passport numbers, driver license numbers, business identification, taxation identifiers, etc.

3.caption: Financial
3.description: Any financially-related sensitive information or Cardholder Data (CHD). E.g., banking account numbers, credit card numbers, International Banking Account Numbers (IBAN), SWIFT codes, etc.

4.caption: Business
4.description: Any business-specific sensitive data such as intellectual property, trademarks, copyrights, human resource data, Board of Directors meeting minutes, and similar.

5.caption: Military and Law Enforcement
5.description: Any mission-specific sensitive data for military, law enforcement, or other government agencies such as specifically classified data, weapon systems information, or other planning data.

6.caption: Security
6.description: Any sensitive security-related data such as passwords, passkeys, IP addresses, API keys, credentials and similar secrets. E.g., AWS Access Secret Key, SaaS API Keys, user passwords, database credentials, etc.

99.caption: Other
99.description: Any other type of data classification or a multi-variate classification made up of several other classification categories.

classifier_details.caption: Classifier Details
classifier_details.description: Describes details about the classifier used for data classification.

confidentiality.caption: Confidentiality
confidentiality.description: The file content confidentiality, normalized to the confidentiality_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidentiality_id.caption: Confidentiality ID
confidentiality_id.description: The normalized identifier of the file content confidentiality indicator.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidentiality is not mapped. See the confidentiality attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

discovery_details.caption: Discovery Details
discovery_details.description: Details about the data discovered by classification job.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: Details about the data policy that governs data handling and security measures related to classification.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The source URL pointing towards the full classification job details.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The resultant status of the classification job normalized to the caption of the status_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

status_details.caption: Status Details
status_details.description: The contextual description of the status, status_id value.

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status identifier of the classification job.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification job type id is not mapped.

1.caption: Complete
1.description: The classification job completed for the evaluated resource.

2.caption: Partial
2.description: The classification job partially completed for the evaluated resource.

3.caption: Fail
3.description: The classification job failed for the evaluated resource.

total.caption: Total
total.description: The total count of discovered entities, by the classification job.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the classification job.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The Device object represents an addressable computer system or host, which is typically connected to a computer network and participates in the transmission or processing of data within the computer network.
device.name: device

name.caption: Name
name.description:
The alternate device name, ordinarily as assigned by an administrator.

Note: The Name could be any other string that helps to identify the device, such as a phone number; for example 310-555-1234.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the device. For example the Windows TargetSID or AWS EC2 ARN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

container.caption: Container
container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

namespace_pid.caption: Namespace PID
namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

agent_list.caption: Agent List
agent_list.description: A list of agent objects associated with a device, endpoint, or resource.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The network domain where the device resides. For example: work.example.com.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.caption: Network Interface Name
interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The device IP address, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the device.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.caption: MAC Vendor
mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The device type. For example: unknown, server, desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, virtual, browser, or other.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone
zone.description: The network zone or LAN segment.

autoscale_uid.caption: Autoscale UID
autoscale_uid.description: The unique identifier of the cloud autoscale configuration.

boot_time.caption: Boot Time
boot_time.description: The time the system was booted.

boot_uid.caption: Boot UID
boot_uid.description: A unique identifier of the device that changes after every reboot. For example, the value of /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id from Linux's procfs.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the device was known to have been created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the device, ordinarily as reported by the operating system.

eid.caption: EID
eid.description: An Embedded Identity Document, is a unique serial number that identifies an eSIM-enabled device.

first_seen_time.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

groups.caption: Groups
groups.description: The group names to which the device belongs. For example: ["Windows Laptops", "Engineering"].

hypervisor.caption: Hypervisor
hypervisor.description: The name of the hypervisor running on the device. For example, Xen, VMware, Hyper-V, VirtualBox, etc.

iccid.caption: ICCID
iccid.description: The Integrated Circuit Card Identification of a mobile device. Typically it is a unique 18 to 22 digit number that identifies a SIM card.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The image used as a template to run the virtual machine.

imei.caption: IMEI
imei.description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity that is associated with the device.

imei_list.caption: IMEI List
imei_list.description: The International Mobile Equipment Identity values that are associated with the device.

is_backed_up.caption: Back Ups Configured
is_backed_up.description: Indicates whether the device or resource has a backup enabled, such as an automated snapshot or a cloud backup. For example, this is indicated by the cloudBackupEnabled value within JAMF Pro mobile devices or the registration of an AWS ARN with the AWS Backup service.

is_compliant.caption: Compliant Device
is_compliant.description: The event occurred on a compliant device.

is_managed.caption: Managed Device
is_managed.description: The event occurred on a managed device.

is_mobile_account_active.caption: Mobile Account Active
is_mobile_account_active.description: Indicates whether the device has an active mobile account. For example, this is indicated by the itunesStoreAccountActive value within JAMF Pro mobile devices.

is_personal.caption: Personal Device
is_personal.description: The event occurred on a personal device.

is_shared.caption: Shared Device
is_shared.description: The event occurred on a shared device.

is_supervised.caption: Supervised Device
is_supervised.description: The event occurred on a supervised device. Devices that are supervised are typically mobile devices managed by a Mobile Device Management solution and are restricted from specific behaviors such as Apple AirDrop.

is_trusted.caption: Trusted Device
is_trusted.description: The event occurred on a trusted device.

last_seen_time.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

meid.caption: MEID
meid.description: The Mobile Equipment Identifier. It's a unique number that identifies a Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) mobile device.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model of the device. For example ThinkPad X1 Carbon.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the device was last known to have been modified.

network_interfaces.caption: Network Interfaces
network_interfaces.description:
The physical or virtual network interfaces that are associated with the device, one for each unique MAC address/IP address/hostname/name combination.

Note: The first element of the array is the network information that pertains to the event.

org.caption: Organization
org.description: Organization and org unit related to the device.

os_machine_uuid.caption: OS Machine UUID
os_machine_uuid.description: The operating system assigned Machine ID. In Windows, this is the value stored at the registry path: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid. In Linux, this is stored in the file: /etc/machine-id.

peripheral_devices.caption: Peripheral Device
peripheral_devices.description: The peripheral devices that are attached or connected to the device.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The region where the virtual machine is located. For example, an AWS Region.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

udid.caption: Unique Device Identifier
udid.description: The Apple assigned Unique Device Identifier (UDID). For iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS devices, this is the UDID. For macOS devices, it is the Provisioning UDID. For example: 00008020-008D4548007B4F26

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: An alternate unique identifier of the device if any. For example the ActiveDirectory DN.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The vendor for the device. For example Dell or Lenovo.

boot_time_dt.caption: Boot Time
boot_time_dt.description: The time the system was booted.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the device was known to have been created.

first_seen_time_dt.caption: First Seen
first_seen_time_dt.description: The initial discovery time of the device.

last_seen_time_dt.caption: Last Seen
last_seen_time_dt.description: The most recent discovery time of the device.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the device was last known to have been modified.

device_hw_info.caption: Device Hardware Info
device_hw_info.description: The Device Hardware Information object contains details and specifications of the physical components that make up a device. This information provides an overview of the hardware capabilities, configuration, and characteristics of the device.
device_hw_info.name: device_hw_info

bios_ver.caption: BIOS Version
bios_ver.description: The BIOS version. For example: LENOVO G5ETA2WW (2.62).

chassis.caption: Chassis
chassis.description: The chassis type describes the system enclosure or physical form factor. For example, as described for a Windows chassis type.

cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The total number of processor cores across all installed CPUs on the system. For per-CPU core detail, use cpu_info_list.

cpu_architecture.caption: CPU Architecture
cpu_architecture.description: The CPU architecture, normalized to the caption of the cpu_architecture_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the source.

cpu_architecture_id.caption: CPU Architecture ID
cpu_architecture_id.description: The normalized identifier of the CPU architecture.

1.caption: x86
1.description: CPU uses the x86 ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

2.caption: ARM
2.description: CPU uses the ARM ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

3.caption: RISC-V
3.description: CPU uses the RISC-V ISA. For bitness, refer to cpu_bits.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The CPU architecture is not mapped. See the cpu_architecture attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

cpu_bits.caption: CPU Bits
cpu_bits.description: The cpu architecture, the number of bits used for addressing in memory. For example: 32 or 64.

cpu_cores.caption: CPU Cores
cpu_cores.description: The number of processor cores in all installed processors. For Example: 42.

cpu_count.caption: CPU Count
cpu_count.description: The number of physical processors on a system. For per-CPU detail, use cpu_info_list.

cpu_info_list.caption: CPU Information
cpu_info_list.description: A list of cpu_info objects, each describing a physical CPU package installed in the device. Use with cpu_count.

cpu_speed.caption: Processor Speed
cpu_speed.description: The speed of the processor in Mhz. For Example: 4200.

cpu_type.caption: Processor Type
cpu_type.description: The processor type. For example: x86 Family 6 Model 37 Stepping 5.

desktop_display.caption: Desktop Display
desktop_display.description: The desktop display affiliated with the event

gpu_count.caption: GPU Count
gpu_count.description: The number of graphics processors on a system. For per-GPU detail, use gpu_info_list.

gpu_info_list.caption: GPU information
gpu_info_list.description: A list of GPU objects describing the hardware properties of each graphics processor installed on the device. Use with gpu_count.

ram_size.caption: RAM Size
ram_size.description: The total amount of installed RAM, in Megabytes. For example: 2048.

uuid.caption: UUID
uuid.description: The device manufacturer assigned universally unique hardware identifier. For SMBIOS compatible devices such as those running Linux and Windows, it is the UUID member of the System Information structure in the SMBIOS information. For macOS devices, it is the Hardware UUID (also known as IOPlatformUUID in the I/O Registry).
